dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: On a 40+ file PR the story produces six or seven chapters that each read fine but carry no discrimination, so Nick skims, approves, and feels uneasy — a stated failure from real use, not a hypothesis.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Two headline numbers: zero collapse-safety violations across every recorded fixture narrative, and at least 40% of narrated diff lines collapsed on the large-PR fixture.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Every gate is a pass-count-guarded `bun test` needing no provider and no tokens; the model-in-the-loop check is an explicitly-labelled manual eval probe.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: Repo sourcing settled on cached tarball snapshots after the daemon was found to have no checkout-resolution mechanism at all; the video's changeKind/primitives/mermaid path was weighed and rejected with reasons.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: The readingPlan precedent is resolved by gating collapse to positive evidence, and the daemon-parity goal is resolved by a snapshot path that behaves identically in both interfaces rather than degrading in one.

problem: Reviewing a large PR in Diff Dad produces six or seven chapters that each read well in isolation and give no sense of which two or three actually decide whether to approve. The result is a skim, an approval, and unease. The story is a nicer-looking full diff rather than a triage.

The signals that could fix this are wrong or unused. `narrative/risk.ts:170-180` computes inbound references only among files already inside the diff, so blast radius today means 'how many other changed files import you' rather than how many unchanged files do. `generateNarrative` is called with `fileTree: []` at every production site (`cli.ts:330`, `server.ts:364`, `daemon/daemon.ts:262`), so the model has never seen anything outside the PR. Every fixture in `eval/fixtures/` declares `expectedHotspots` and nothing in `eval/judge.ts` reads it; the only ranking check, `chaptersOrderedByRisk`, asserts the risk labels are non-increasing, which a narrative that labels everything low passes.

Large PRs also lose content silently. `MAX_TOTAL_DIFF_LINES = 12000` causes `prompt.ts:495` to drop whole files, and `engine.ts:76-80` prints that warning to the terminal only. In the browser there is no indication that the story was built from a partial diff.

There is a live precedent for how this fails. The LLM `readingPlan` was built, shipped, and then pulled from the UI because 'most of the time it just says to read the chapters in order.' A collapse boundary is the same genre of meta-output and will meet the same fate unless every collapse is backed by a fact the chapter list does not already imply.
goals: Zero collapse-safety violations: no file listed in a fixture's `expectedHotspots` ever appears inside a collapsed chapter, across every recorded fixture narrative, enforced by a test that fails the build.
At least 40% of narrated diff lines sit inside collapsed chapters on the large-PR fixture, measured in lines rather than chapter count so tiny-chapter collapsing cannot game it.

Inbound-reference counts reflect the whole repository rather than only the diff, and the risk score's centrality term discriminates across that wider range instead of saturating at its current cap of ten.
Collapse never renders without positive evidence: an input with no mechanical signals produces zero collapsed chapters and no divider, leaving the story visually identical to today.
Repo context resolves identically in `dad review` and in the daemon, with the unavailable state reserved for a repository above the size cap or a failed fetch, and naming which.
Prompt-budget truncation is visible in the browser: when files are dropped or truncated before the model sees them, the review says so instead of looking complete.

mvp.item: Repo snapshot: fetch the base ref tarball into a size-capped, age-bounded cache under the regenerable cache dir, extract with path-traversal and symlink guards, and build an import index in the same pass
mvp.reason: Indexing during extraction avoids a second full read and removes any dependency on ripgrep or git being installed; the cache dir choice follows the durable-versus-regenerable split already documented in paths.ts

mvp.item: Repo-wide inbound references in risk.ts, with the score's centrality term rescaled so it still discriminates once counts are no longer bounded by the diff
mvp.reason: computeScore currently caps the term at `Math.min(inboundRefs, 10) * 4`, which repo-wide counts saturate for nearly every non-leaf file, turning centrality into a constant and reproducing the exact no-discrimination symptom the project exists to fix

mvp.item: Pure collapse-selection function over (chapters, risk signals, repo context) returning which chapters collapse and the one-line evidence for each, computed at serve time and never persisted
mvp.reason: Purity is what makes the safety gate free and deterministic, and serve-time computation avoids a cache-key defect: narrativeCachePath() carries no repo-state component, so a narrative generated while context was unavailable would keep collapsing nothing at that SHA forever

mvp.item: Large-PR fixture (40+ files) with ground-truth hotspots, plus recorded narratives for it and the four existing fixtures
mvp.reason: selectCollapsible needs chapters and EvalFixture carries none, so without recorded narratives the safety and compression gates have no input and would report a vacuous pass

mvp.item: Collapse rendering in the story view: one divider before the first collapsed chapter, the evidence line on each, and an unavailable notice when repo context could not be resolved
mvp.reason: Chapter.tsx:271 already owns a `collapsed` state seeded from `reviewed`, so this seeds that existing state rather than introducing a second driver; the unavailable notice is the only surface that delivers the repo-context goal

full.item: Score expectedHotspots in eval/judge.ts and report placement per run in EvalRun and the aggregate
full.reason: The ground-truth field is declared on every fixture and read by nothing; wiring it is what makes the manual eval probe worth running after a prompt change

full.item: Prompt-cap statistics plumbed from the planner through the engine to the narrative API, and a truncation banner in the web UI
full.reason: runPlanner returns only {plan, provider, usage} and NarrativeGenerationResult only {narrative, provider}, so the stats are computed and discarded today; a story built from a truncated diff currently looks identical to a complete one

full.item: Collapse state and the unavailable notice carried through the daemon's own Hono app and unit persistence
full.reason: The daemon serves from daemon/app.ts with its own routes and persists units through units/store.ts, so nothing reaches the daemon drill-in by way of the CLI server

stretch.item: Expandable caller list per chapter: click the evidence line to see which unchanged files import the changed module
stretch.reason: Turns the evidence from a claim into something checkable without leaving the review; the import index already holds the data

stretch.item: Snapshot prefetch on daemon poll, so context is warm before a review is opened
stretch.reason: Removes first-open latency, but only matters once the snapshot path has proven itself in normal use

outOfScope.reason: Without a primitives manifest the model guesses, and 'adds a primitive' degrades into 'adds a file', which risk.ts already approximates from churn plus new-file

outOfScope.reason: Kent reports his own system map needs work, and the flow diagram is unproven against the stated triage problem

outOfScope.item: A separate ranking pass that reorders chapters
outOfScope.reason: prompt.ts:229 already instructs the model to order by risk descending with mechanical changes last; collapse happens in place, and reordering a five-element list adds a mechanism that duplicates one the pipeline performs

outOfScope.item: Local checkout detection as a fast path when the current directory is already the repo
outOfScope.reason: A second provider means two sets of edge cases and results that differ by where the command was run; the snapshot path is uniform and the cache makes the repeat cost negligible

computeRisk stores one integer per file and formatRiskHints prints it as inbound=N, so file-and-module granularity is all any MVP consumer reads; symbol granularity is only needed once the stretch-tier caller list is scheduled

outOfScope.reason: This project makes truncation visible rather than adjusting it; retuning caps is a different investigation with its own cost curve

decisions.decision: Source repo context from cached tarball snapshots, uniform in the CLI and the daemon
decisions.rejected: Local git grep against a checkout, with an explicit unavailable state when the repo is not on disk
decisions.reason: Reversed after the hidden-dependency critic found the daemon has no checkout-resolution mechanism at all — units/store.ts:133 mints an empty worktreePath that nothing sets, launchd.ts:87-112 sets no WorkingDirectory, and inferRepoFromGit reads cwd — so the local-git plan would have reported unavailable on 100% of daemon PRs, against a standing daemon-parity goal

decisions.decision: Fetch a tarball rather than cloning
decisions.rejected: git clone --depth 1, and a bare mirror per repo
decisions.reason: Grep needs file contents, not history; a shallow clone drags an object store that is never read, and --filter=blob:none is actively wrong because grep would trigger a network fetch per file

decisions.decision: Build the import index during extraction and persist it beside the snapshot
decisions.rejected: Shelling out to ripgrep or git grep at query time
decisions.reason: One pass over files already being written, no dependency on a binary that may not be installed, and caller lookup becomes a map read rather than a scan

decisions.decision: Compute collapse state at serve time and never persist it
decisions.rejected: Carrying collapse fields through the narrative cache and normalization
decisions.reason: narrativeCachePath() keys on owner-repo-number-sha-metaHash-provider with no repo-state component, so a narrative generated while context was unavailable would keep collapsing nothing at that SHA forever, silently defeating the safety and compression goals

decisions.decision: Collapse chapters in place, in the order the model already produced
decisions.rejected: A separate ranking pass that reorders chapters before drawing the boundary
decisions.reason: prompt.ts:229 already instructs risk-descending order with mechanical changes last, and chaptersOrderedByRisk asserts it; a reorder over a list capped at seven is machinery duplicating existing behavior

decisions.decision: Author the large fixture and all recorded narratives in the same phase that owns the safety gate
decisions.rejected: Tiering the large fixture as Full and authoring it in a later, non-blocking phase
decisions.reason: Three critics independently found the same circularity: the gate needs chapters, EvalFixture carries none, and the only planned recorded narrative lived in a phase that listed the gate's phase as its prerequisite

decisions.decision: Guard every name-filtered test command with a pass-count check
decisions.reason: A -t filter matching nothing exits 0, so three of the goals hung on checks that pass whether or not the test was ever written; separately `-t cap` matched the existing recap tests at server.test.ts:169 and :175 and passed on main before any work

decisions.decision: Rescale the centrality term in computeScore
decisions.rejected: Leaving Math.min(inboundRefs, 10) * 4 and simply widening what inboundRefs counts
decisions.reason: Repo-wide counts saturate that cap for essentially every non-leaf file, turning the term into a constant 40 and reproducing the no-discrimination symptom the project exists to fix

decisions.decision: Run both test suites in the acceptance command
decisions.rejected: `bun run test && bun run typecheck` alone
decisions.reason: Root `test` is `bun test packages/cli/src/__tests__/` and never touches the 11 vitest files under packages/web/src, which is where the only new UI code lives

decisions.decision: Build repo context plus collapse signals
decisions.rejected: The video's path: changeKind classification, a primitives manifest, and mermaid change-flow diagrams
decisions.reason: That approach works because the authoring agent already holds the repo; Diff Dad reconstructs from an API response, so the classification would rest on structure it cannot see

decisions.decision: The hard gate is a unit test over a pure selection function; the eval harness is a manual probe
decisions.rejected: Asserting on the eval baseline as the blocking gate
decisions.reason: A gate that needs a configured provider and spends tokens per run gets disabled, and then there is no gate at all

decisions.decision: Measure compression in narrated diff lines
decisions.reason: Chapter counts are gameable by collapsing many tiny chapters while the two open ones still hold most of the code

decisions.decision: Collapse engages only when positive evidence exists for that chapter
decisions.rejected: Always rendering the boundary, and gating additionally on PR size
decisions.reason: readingPlan was pulled from the UI for being always-on meta-output that usually said nothing; a size threshold adds a number to tune without adding safety

phases.title: Repo snapshot and import index
phases.notes: Tarball fetch for the PR's base ref, guarded extraction into a size-capped and age-bounded cache, and an import index built in the same pass. The index stores the caller file list per module, not just a count, since the Stretch-tier caller list reads it. Replace risk.ts's diff-internal inbound-ref computation with repo-wide counts and rescale the centrality term (log, like churn at risk.ts:152) so it does not saturate. computeRisk runs inside the synchronous prompt builders at prompt.ts:589, :603 and :679, so resolved context must be threaded as a generateNarrative parameter through planner, writer and engine, and supplied at all three production call sites. risk.test.ts:66 asserts the behavior being replaced and must be rewritten.

phases.title: Collapse selection, cap stats, and fixtures
phases.notes: The safety-critical phase, and it owns its own inputs. A pure selectCollapsible(chapters, risks, repoContext) returning collapse decisions with evidence sentences, computed at serve time and absent from the cache. Authors the 40+ file large-refactor fixture, registers it in the hand-maintained FIXTURES array, and records narratives for it and the four existing fixtures so the safety and compression gates have real chapters to run against. Also plumbs PromptCapStats out of runPlanner (which currently returns only plan, provider and usage) and onto NarrativeGenerationResult, since Phase 3 is forbidden from editing narrative internals.

phases.title: Review surfaces
prereqs: Collapse selection, cap stats, and fixtures
phases.notes: Divider, evidence lines, unavailable notice and truncation banner. packages/web declares its own NarrativeResponse rather than importing the CLI's, so the web-side type must gain the fields or typecheck fails. Chapter.tsx:271 already owns a collapsed state seeded from `reviewed`, with a force-collapse effect at :273-276 and a grid-rows animation at :598-621 — seed that state rather than adding a second driver, and state precedence when a chapter is both reviewed and collapsible. The daemon serves from its own Hono app and persists units separately, so both paths need wiring. Stretch tier is in scope: the evidence line expands to the caller file list from Phase 1's index, and the daemon prefetches snapshots on poll so context is warm before a review is opened.

phases.title: Eval hotspot scoring
prereqs: Collapse selection, cap stats, and fixtures
phases.notes: Wire the dead expectedHotspots field into judge.ts and report placement per run in EvalRun and the aggregate. Line compression is deliberately not added here: the deterministic collapse test already measures it for free on the same fixture, and duplicating it inside a provider-backed probe would grow the baseline for a number no criterion reads. safe-rename declares an empty expectedHotspots, so scoring must treat that as not-applicable rather than as a miss.

execution.agentTeamPrompt: Phases 3 (Review surfaces) and 4 (Eval hotspot scoring) are both blocked only by Phase 2 and touch disjoint files, so run them in parallel once Phase 2 lands. Phase 3 owns packages/web, packages/cli/src/server.ts, packages/cli/src/daemon and packages/cli/src/units. Phase 4 owns packages/cli/src/eval, except eval/types.ts which Phase 2 has already extended — read its current shape before editing. Neither phase may edit packages/cli/src/narrative: that shape is frozen by Phase 2, and needing a change there means stopping and revising Phase 2's spec rather than patching around it.
